questions_and_answers.question_text: Give the Chinese names for Monday through Saturday.
Which day of the week is NOT formed with a number?
Where does -jǐ appear in the word xīngqījǐ?
What is the literal meaning of xīngqījǐ?
Write the Chinese for "We are leaving on Sunday."
Which position does jǐ occupy, whether at the beginning or the end of a word?

answers.answer_text: It occupies the position of a number and acts like a number.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give three examples of jǐ- appearing at the beginning of a word.
What is the Chinese for Sunday?
Write the Chinese for "No, we arrived on Friday."

answers.answer_text: Bú shi, wǒmen shi Xīngqīwǔ dàode.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which construction is used in exchange 2 to focus on the day of arrival?

articles.text:
2. A: Nǐmen shi Xīngqīsì dàode ma?          Did you arrive on Thursday?
   B: Bú shi, wǒmen shi Xīngqīwǔ            No, we arrived on Friday.
      dàode.

3. A: Nǐmen xīngqījǐ zǒu?                   What day of the week are you
                                            leaving?
   B: Wǒmen Xīngqītiān zǒu.                 We are leaving on Sunday.

Notes on Nos. 2-3

Days of the week:

xīngqījǐ?          (what day of the week?)
Xīngqīyī           (Monday)
Xīngqīèr           (Tuesday)
Xīngqīsān          (Wednesday)
Xīngqīsì           (Thursday)
Xīngqīwǔ           (Friday)
Xīngqīliù          (Saturday)
Xīngqītiān         (Sunday)

Until now, you have always seen jǐ-, "how many," at the beginning of a word (jǐge háizi, jǐwèi xiānsheng, jǐhào). In xīngqījǐ, -jǐ is at the end of the word. In both places, jǐ occupies the position of a number and acts like a number: xīngqījǐ, "what number day of the week?"
